records.reason: The abstract names Zhang and Arvey’s 2009 retrospective empirical study and its male-adult association between recalled adolescent antisocial rule-breaking and entrepreneurship. The present study uses prospective longitudinal cohort data and reports the corresponding positive prediction among men, so it directly retests that finding. The supplied shipped original (row 1322) is Zhang et al. (2009), “The genetic basis of entrepreneurship: Effects of gender and personality,” a distinct work and not the cited rule-breaking study. Prior adjudication: none.
records.location: Abstract, opening sentence (original finding) and regression-results sentence (new cohort test).
records.omission_quote: Regression results, which controlled for early socioeconomic background and intellectual competencies, indeed identified early antisocial rule-breaking behavior in adolescence as a valid positive predictor of a subsequent entrepreneurial career in adulthood in men (but not in women).
records.identity_quote: Drawing from Zhang and Arvey's retrospective study [Zhang, Z. & Arvey, R.D. (2009). Rule breaking in adolescence and entrepreneurial status: An empirical investigation. Journal of Business Venturing, 24(5), 436–447], which found a link between entrepreneurship status of male adults and their recalled early antisocial rule-breaking behavior in adolescence,
